title: Replace a car's wiper blade: hold the sprung wiper arm off the windscreen while the other hand swaps the blade
instruction: Replace the wiper blade: with one hand lift the wiper arm off the windscreen and hold it up; with the other slide the old blade along the arm toward its pivot, off the hook, and drop it in the grey scrap tray, then hook the new blade from the cardboard tray onto the arm and slide it toward the arm's tip until it clicks in. Lower the arm gently back onto the glass without letting it snap down, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Changing wiper blades is one of the most common jobs in car servicing, fleet maintenance and quick-lube shops. The arm is sprung hard against the glass: one hand has to hold it up while the other unhooks the old blade and hooks on the new one, and an arm that slips and snaps down can crack the windscreen.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) The front of a car, fixed: a black ABS cowl panel 27 to 31 cm forward and 4 cm tall, then a windscreen of tinted laminated glass rising away from the arms at 20 degrees from its bottom edge (31 cm forward), 30 cm long along its slope and 54 cm across (from 25 cm right to 29 cm left of the centre line), on a red-painted steel body with red pillars at both sides and the roof's edge at the top; the passenger's wiper, parked higher up the glass, is fixed. (2) The driver's wiper, parked along the bottom of the glass 34.5 cm forward: a black-painted steel arm 27 cm long, its pivot under a black cap 17 cm left of the centre line, reaching to 10 cm right of it, its tip bent down into a hook. A spring presses it onto the glass (holding it lifted 15 degrees takes about 0.2 N m); it lifts up to 35 degrees. (3) The old blade, hooked on under the arm: a black steel frame 24 cm long, 1.2 cm wide and 1.4 cm tall on a worn grey rubber strip, 30 g, its dark grey adapter at its middle, 25 cm from the pivot (8 cm right of the centre line). (4) A new blade, the same with black rubber and a silver adapter, standing upright in a kraft cardboard tray (5 x 28 cm) 22.5 cm forward, its middle 8 cm right of the centre line. (5) A grey polypropylene scrap tray, 6 x 29 cm inside and 3.5 cm tall, 14 cm forward, its middle 15 cm right of the centre line. A hooked blade slides along the arm only while the arm is lifted at least 8 degrees (on the glass it is held); slid 2 cm toward the pivot it comes off the hook. A free blade held in line with the arm (within 30 degrees), within 1.5 cm of the hook's line and 0.5 to 1.6 cm short of its end catches on the hook; slid to within 4 mm of the hook's end it clicks in. The hook takes one blade at a time. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. 0.0 if the wiper arm ever snapped down onto the glass (reaching within 4 degrees of resting on it faster than 1.5 rad/s). Otherwise 1.0: the old blade off the arm and in the scrap tray, the new blade hooked on and clicked in (within 4 mm of the hook's end), the arm down on the glass (within 3 degrees of resting on it) and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre, TCP, within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: the old blade in the scrap tray and the new one clicked in, otherwise; 0.25: the old blade in the scrap tray; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the wiper arm and both blades still.
reset_notes: Hook the worn blade back on the arm with the arm on the glass, and stand the new blade back in its cardboard tray.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the arm is a rigid bar on a sprung hinge; the hook is a slide joint along the arm that the task file switches on and off by distance (catch, unhook, click), with no latch tab to press; blades and rubber do not flex; the car is fixed. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
